question_text: If ²²Cᵣ is the largest binomial coefficient in the expansion of (1 + x)²², find the value of ¹³Cᵣ.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find ¹³Cᵣ — how the largest coefficient of (1 + x)²² fixes r, and how ¹³C₁₁ is evaluated.
insider_note: n = 22 is even, so r = 11, and ¹³C₁₁ is read as ¹³C₂ by symmetry. Computing it from factorials by hand is the long way to the same one mark.

steps.label: Find r from the largest coefficient
steps.margin_note: First mark. n = 22 is even, so the largest coefficient is the middle one ²²C₁₁; hence r = 11.
steps.memory_tip: n = 22 is even, so the largest coefficient is the single middle one, ²²C₁₁, and r = 11.
lines: n = 22 is even, so the largest coefficient

recall.must_convey: That n = 22 is even so the largest coefficient is ²²C₁₁, which gives r = 11.
accept: n is twenty two which is even so the largest coefficient is twenty two C eleven and r is eleven
the middle coefficient of an even power is the largest so r is n by two which is eleven
twenty two even kabatti largest twenty two C eleven, r eleven
r is half of twenty two

steps.why: The question gives r only through a fact about (1 + x)²²; recognising the middle coefficient is the whole first mark.
common_mistakes: Giving two values of r as if n were odd.

steps.label: Evaluate ¹³C₁₁
steps.margin_note: Second mark. ¹³C₁₁ = ¹³C₂ because 11 + 2 = 13; ¹³C₂ = (13·12)/(1·2) = 78.
steps.memory_tip: ¹³C₁₁ = ¹³C₂ because 11 + 2 = 13, so it is just (13 × 12)/2 = 78.

accept: thirteen C eleven is thirteen C two which is thirteen into twelve by two, seventy eight
use n C r equals n C n minus r to get thirteen C two
thirteen C eleven ante thirteen C two, seventy eight

steps.why: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ turns an eleven-factor product into a two-factor one.
common_mistakes: Computing ¹³C₁₁ as 13·12·…·3 over 11! by hand.
